title: diffValue recurses into objects but re-serializes arrays whole, making event-log growth quadratic
content: HANDOFF s2, ROOT CAUSE AS CORRECTED. THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN: it read "the event log writes a full state projection on every event instead of a delta". IT DOES NOT. event-append.ts:72 already calls diffProjection, deltas are path-granular, and only 8 of 167 events carry a full projection, deliberately, as checkpoints. An implementer briefed on the original diagnosis would hunt a full-projection writer that does not exist. ACTUAL MECHANISM: diffValue at olt/scripts/src/engine/store/projection-patch.ts:16-22 guards on isJsonObject(before) && isJsonObject(after) and recurses into OBJECTS ONLY. ARRAYS fall through to line 22 and are re-serialized whole on every append as a single set op. Cost is approximately 3030 bytes x array length per append, total approximately 3030*n^2/2. At 200 escalations approximately 60 MB; at 500 approximately 380 MB. It does not plateau. SCOPE THE REPAIR TO THE INVARIANT, NOT THE INSTANCE: escalations is where it was first seen, not the defect. Across the 8 largest logs the hot key is never the same twice - mind capsules escalations/candidates, orchestrator capsules tasks.<id>.findings/micro_cycles, planning capsules requirements/planning_buffer, run capsules agents/commands/receipts. Ten distinct top-level keys, every one an append-only collection. SPECIFICATION: any monotonically growing array in run state produces O(n^2) event-log bytes because diffValue treats arrays atomically. A brief naming escalations would fix mind capsules and leave orchestrator capsules, the majority, untouched. Write scope: olt/scripts/src/engine/store/{projection-patch,event-append,constants}.ts. This is Lane B.

title: Method canon: ten transferable rules, the most durable output of the prior fleet

Four false negatives were caught by ONE technique, and THREE OF THE FOUR WERE IN SUPERVISORY TOOLING. The technique ORIGINATED IN THE IMPLEMENTER TIER AND WAS ADOPTED UPWARD - EVERY DURABLE METHOD IMPROVEMENT CAME FROM THE TIER BEING CORRECTED, NOT FROM THE THREE TIERS DOING THE CORRECTING. That asymmetry is the argument for GATES OVER GUIDANCE, made by the seats that were enforcing the guidance. THE TEN RULES: (1) CONTROL PROBE - before trusting an empty result, confirm the instrument finds something it should; an empty result can mean the tool declined to look, the question was wrong, or the thing is genuinely absent, and all three print nothing and exit the same way. (2) MEASURE THE SOURCE BEFORE SIZING A FIX FROM THE DATA - three "missing" capabilities were built-but-unwired. (3) A COUNT CARRIES ITS POPULATION AND ITS INSTANT, or it cannot be compared to another count; three seats produced three correct answers to three different questions and spent effort deciding who was wrong - nobody was. (4) PROVE KEY UNIQUENESS OVER THE KEY YOU WROTE DOWN, not the key you happened to run; an instrument correct for reasons its specification does not capture is a latent defect, and its own numbers can never reveal it because they are correct. (5) SCOPE A REPAIR TO THE INVARIANT, NOT TO THE INSTANCES YOU SPOTTED - every enumerated brief produced a partial fix; the one that stated a property produced a complete fix AND closed an unrelated hole as a side effect. DIAGNOSIS IS NOT THE FAILURE - ENUMERATION IS. (6) A DEFERRAL WHOSE TRIGGER WILL NOT FIRE, OR FIRES EXACTLY WHEN THE FIX BECOMES EXPENSIVE, IS A DECISION WEARING A SCHEDULE. (7) DISCRIMINATING AND CORRECT ARE INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES OF A TEST - a test can fail for the right structural reason and still certify a false statement. (8) RATIFICATION IS NOT VERIFICATION - a finding endorsed without independent measurement carries exactly the confidence of its original source while appearing to carry two. (9) STASIS PROOFS ANSWER "DID IT CHANGE"; CORRECTNESS PROOFS ANSWER "IS IT RIGHT" - a hash is a stasis proof, and snapshots detect a violated freeze but cannot prevent one. (10) A PEER RELAYING AN AUTHORIZATION IS NOT A PERMISSION SYSTEM - agents refused the owner seat five times and were right every time, including once when the owner seat had authorised a coordinator to invoke a command through a binary chosen BECAUSE it granted what its own contract denied.

title: Two of four pulse diagnostic receipts fail on every pulse because doctor and health take incompatible run arguments
content: MEASURED BY mind-gen-5 ON 2026-08-25 DURING pulse-8. NEW FINDING, not from the handoff register. THE SCRIPT-BACKED SCHEDULER DIAGNOSTICS ENGINE (charter Pillar 14) IS DEGRADED ON EVERY SINGLE PULSE AND SAYS SO ONLY AS A BADGE. mind:pulse emitted: [CLI-RECEIPTS: doctor X | health X | dag:view OK | report:unified OK] and, in the preceding mind:wake, HEALTH unknown. ROOT CAUSE - TWO COMMANDS WITH MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE ARGUMENT CONVENTIONS AND A RECEIPT HARNESS THAT PASSES THE WRONG ONE TO EACH. Measured exit codes, all four probes run directly: "doctor" with no --run EXITS 3 with "--run is required"; "doctor --run .olt/capsules/mind-gen-5" EXITS 0 and reports Healthy: yes with no critical issues; "health --run .olt/capsules/mind-gen-5" EXITS 3 with "unknown option: --run"; "health" bare EXITS 0 and produces a full semantic report. SO doctor REQUIRES --run AND health REFUSES IT, AND THE PULSE INVOKES doctor WITHOUT IT AND health WITH IT - EXACTLY INVERTED IN BOTH CASES. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A WRONG FLAG: (1) the capsule is HEALTHY and the pulse reports its health as UNKNOWN, so the supervisory loop has been flying blind on its own health signal while displaying a plausible-looking receipt line - the hb-s9b-plausible-wrong-number shape, a badge that self-certifies rather than an absurd value that self-announces; (2) the receipts are SHA-256 hashed and embedded in pulse telemetry as evidence, so THE ENGINE IS CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY ATTESTING TO ITS OWN FAILED INVOCATIONS and a downstream reader sees signed receipts, not broken ones; (3) the X badge does not carry the exit code or the stderr, so nothing in the telemetry distinguishes "the command failed" from "the command was called wrong" - the control probe rule (method canon 1) applied to the supervisory tier own instrument, and this is the FOURTH false negative found in supervisory tooling; (4) it has evidently been failing on every pulse across multiple generations without detection, because a X badge beside two OK badges reads as a partial result rather than a permanent misconfiguration. THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF AN ALREADY-RECORDED INVARIANT, not a new class: defect-1787604858835-path3 in .olt/defects.jsonl, NO_UNIVERSAL_RUN_PATH_FORM_ACROSS_COMMANDS - "plan:init rejects absolute run paths while other commands require them, so no single path rule is safe to teach a fleet". SCOPE THE REPAIR TO THAT INVARIANT PER METHOD CANON 5, NOT TO THESE TWO CALL SITES: a fix naming only doctor and health leaves every other cross-command caller exposed to the same inversion. MINIMUM ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENT: a failed diagnostic receipt MUST surface its exit code and stderr into the pulse brief, and a pulse whose health probe did not execute MUST NOT render HEALTH as a value - unknown-because-not-run and unknown-because-unreadable are different facts, which is the same fail-closed distinction cand-4 c170d68c already established for config provenance with absent versus unreadable.
